answer:
If you have a tension-type headache, treatment typically involves over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen or an NSAID. According to the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3), tension-type headaches are characterized by bilateral, pressing or tightening pain without being aggravating by routine physical activity and can be effectively managed with analgesia and identifying and avoiding triggers such as stress, poor sleep, or dehydration [Tension-Type Headache, International Headache Society, 2018].

For acute migraine treatment, it is suggested that first-line treatments for most patients include NSAIDs or triptans. A combined approach of a triptan with an NSAID may be more effective than either medication alone. Additionally, for individuals who have four or more migraine days per month, preventive therapy should also be considered in addition to acute treatment recommendations [Acute Treatment of Migraine, American Headache Society, 2021].

Please consult a healthcare professional for personalized advice and treatment plans as these guidelines may vary based on individual circumstances.

results.content: Tension-type headache presents as bilateral, pressing or tightening pain of mild to moderate intensity, not aggravated by routine physical activity. First-line treatment is over-the-counter analgesia (acetaminophen or an NSAID) and addressing triggers such as stress, poor sleep, or dehydration.
results.source: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd ed.
